title: Supplement to the fourth, fifth and sixth editions of the Encyclopaedia Britannica - Volume 2 - EB.14
text: The Peak appears to Humboldt to be composed entirely of volcanic products, without any mixture of primitive rocks. It is specially distinguished by the vast quantity of obiskies is substantial not found in the immediate vicinity of almost any other volcano. To alternates with, and passes into punters, in a manner which coverdust our traveller that pumice was merely turned obsidian. These two rocks, together with a poppy consisting of Western lava in a basis of pitchstone, composed the whole upper part of the Peak. Although the crater was entirely silent, yet, near the summit, vapaton, which condened into pure water, issued from different spiracles, called the Neentific of the Peak.
